hero_tagline: Compute at the Horizon of Certainty
section_why_description: Modern scientific computing demands more than correct arithmetic—it demands epistemic integrity. Sounio transitions uncertainty from a post-hoc statistical check into a first-class compiler invariant.
feature_uncertainty_desc: Every measurement carries the exact bounds of its precision. The first-class Knowledge<T> type couples physical values with ISO GUM uncertainty parameters and end-to-end provenance.
feature_propagation_desc: Rigorous, ISO GUM-compliant uncertainty propagation across all mathematical expressions. Express the physical model; the compiler dynamically computes the statistical bounds.
feature_provenance_desc: Data without origin lacks authority. Every computed value maintains a cryptographic trace back to its sensor calibrations, essential for reproducibility and strict regulatory audits.
feature_confidence_desc: When statistical uncertainty violates safety bounds, the compiler mandates mitigation paths or halts execution. The runtime is aware of its own limitations.
feature_domain_desc: Natively integrated medical-grade DSLs for PK/PD modeling (MedLang), functional neuroimaging (fMRI), causal networks, and parallel execution via Kretikos GPU lane.
feature_standards_desc: Engineered from first principles for ISO GUM, ISO 17025, FDA 21 CFR Part 11, and the FAIR data guidelines. Compliance is not an afterthought—it is architectural.
maturity_description: Sounio is in active development. Here's the current maturity of core features to help you understand what's production-ready.
comparison_description: Sounio uniquely combines epistemic computing as a first-class concern with high-performance systems programming.

name_description: Cape Sounion (Σούνιο) stands at the southernmost tip of Attica, where the ancient Temple of Poseidon has watched over the Aegean for 2,500 years. At sunset, its Doric columns catch the last light—the horizon where certainty meets the unknown sea.
name_meaning: Sounio the language embodies this metaphor: computing at the boundary between what we know and what we don't.
